# omni_user_attribute (Data Source)

Looks up a user attribute definition by its reference name.

Attribute definitions cannot be created through the API, only read. Make them in the UI under **Settings > User attributes**, then reference them here so a configuration fails loudly on an instance that is missing one, instead of applying cleanly with row-level security that does nothing.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) The attribute's unique ID.
- `name` (String) The attribute's **Reference** value, for example `tenant_id`.

### Read-Only

- `default_value` (String) Value used when a user has none set. Null when the attribute takes multiple values, because there is more than one: read `default_values` instead.
- `default_values` (List of String) Values used when a user has none set, for an attribute that takes multiple values. A single-valued attribute reports its one default here too, so this is the attribute to read when the shape is not known in advance.
- `description` (String) Description of the attribute and its purpose.
- `label` (String) Display label shown in the UI.
- `multiple_values` (Boolean) Whether the attribute accepts more than one value per user.
- `system` (Boolean) Whether Omni defines and populates this attribute. Do not set a system attribute through `omni_user`: the platform owns the value and will not return it, so every plan would propose setting it again.
- `type` (String) `String` or `Number`. Number attributes are stored as strings for precision.
